checks.name: opens_with_problem
checks.instructions: The plan opens with a concrete problem, failure, or personal situation, not a definition or a product history.
checks.fix: Rewrite the opening around the concrete situation that makes the topic matter. Move any definition or history below the first thing the reader can act on.

checks.name: corporate_language
checks.instructions: The plan contains corporate, marketing, or generic AI assistant phrasing such as 'leverage', 'seamless', 'robust solution', or 'let's dive in'.
checks.fix: Replace corporate and marketing phrasing with plain verbs such as run, set, check, use, and remove. Read the Avoid list in BLOG_VOICE_GUIDE.md first.

checks.name: vague_warnings
checks.instructions: The plan contains a warning or gotcha that does not say what actually goes wrong, such as 'this may cause issues'.
checks.fix: For each warning or gotcha, state the exact failure: what breaks, when, and what the reader sees.

checks.name: voice
checks.instructions: How closely the plan reads like an experienced engineer documenting something they personally tested.
criteria: Generic documentation, marketing copy, or AI assistant prose
Clear and direct but impersonal, it could be anyone's post
Practical, first person where tested, mildly opinionated, candid about tradeoffs
checks.fix: Reread BLOG_VOICE_GUIDE.md and revise toward it: first person only for tested experience, second person for instructions, direct recommendations, honest tradeoffs.

checks.name: mental_model_early
checks.instructions: The plan states one central mental model or TL;DR before its first step, command, or code block.
checks.fix: State the load bearing idea or a TL;DR before the first command.

checks.name: ends_with_takeaway
checks.instructions: The post in the plan ends, or is planned to end, with a short operational takeaway, not a summary that restates the post.
checks.fix: End on the one operational lesson, compressed to a line or two. Cut any summary that restates the post.

checks.name: has_topic_verdict
checks.instructions: The request contains a topic check result with a line labelled Verdict, and that verdict begins with Write, Write symptom first, Fold into, or Skip.
checks.fix: Stop and tell Keith the request has no topic check verdict. Run the topic-check skill, then start the gate again with a request that includes the verdict. Do not write the verdict yourself.

checks.name: verdict_is_skip
checks.instructions: The request contains a topic check verdict, and that verdict is Skip.
checks.fix: Stop. Tell Keith the verdict is Skip and ask whether to drop the post or write what the verdict suggests instead.

checks.name: fold_written_as_new_post
checks.instructions: The request contains a topic check verdict that starts with Fold into, and the plan proposes a new standalone post.
checks.fix: Stop. Tell Keith the verdict says to fold this into an existing post, and ask whether to rework the plan as additions to that post.

checks.name: uses_verdict_strings
checks.instructions: The request's topic check verdict lists exact strings for headings, and the plan's title or headings contain them.
checks.fix: Put the exact strings the verdict lists (error text, command names) into the title or headings.

checks.name: uses_verdict_angle
checks.instructions: The plan takes the angle that the topic check verdict in the request recommends.
checks.fix: Rework the plan around the angle the verdict recommends, or tell Keith why a different angle is better.

checks.name: missing_stated_version
checks.instructions: The request says which platform version the post targets, and the plan's title does not include that version.
checks.fix: Put the platform and version the request targets in the title.

checks.name: invented_demand_numbers
checks.instructions: The plan states search volume or demand numbers that the request does not contain.
checks.fix: Remove every demand or search volume figure the request does not contain.

checks.name: short_shelf_life
checks.instructions: The request or the plan says an upcoming release or package change will make this post wrong within months.
checks.fix: Say in the plan whether the post can ship before the release lands and what will need updating when it does.

checks.name: links_existing_posts
checks.instructions: The plan names at least one existing Peculiar Engineer post it will link to.
checks.fix: Name the existing posts this one links to and which of them should link back.

checks.name: lab_verified
checks.instructions: The plan says its commands were run, or will be run before publishing, on a real machine of the stated platform.
checks.fix: Add the lab verification step: which box, which image, and that every command in the post gets run there before publishing.

checks.name: untested_claims_as_tested
checks.instructions: The plan claims first hand testing or personal experience for something the request does not say was actually tested.
checks.fix: Remove every first person claim of testing or experience the request does not back, or mark it as something to verify in the lab run.

checks.name: contradicts_request
checks.instructions: The plan states a fact, version number, or command output that contradicts the request.
checks.fix: Find each place the plan disagrees with the request on a fact, version, or output, and correct the plan or flag the disagreement for Keith.

checks.name: claims_have_sources
checks.instructions: Each claim in the plan about how a tool behaves names its source: official docs, a man page, or captured output.
checks.fix: Note the source for each behavioural claim: the official doc, the man page, or the lab transcript that shows it.

checks.name: absolute_claims
checks.instructions: The plan makes absolute claims such as 'always works', 'never fails', or 'the best tool' without a stated caveat.
checks.fix: Add the caveat or the case where the claim does not hold.
